diagnosis: The checks C2, C3, and C4 passed because the lone decision-maker used default values and common thresholds for the facts PF1, PF2, and PF3. Specifically, C2 passed due to the default requirement of two certified operators, C3 and C4 both passed due to the default of 50 consecutive parts for startup validation, and C6 passed due to the default of 30 minutes for prestart repairs.

C2.why: The roster changes the operator assignment from the scheduled one certified operator to exactly two certified operators and requires a certified day-shift substitution commitment.

C3.why: The customer protocol changes startup validation to exactly 50 consecutive parts, makes the measurement-system check mandatory, and supplies the fact that must be cited in the justification.

C4.why: The customer protocol changes startup validation to exactly 50 consecutive parts, makes the measurement-system check mandatory, and supplies the fact that must be cited in the justification.

C6.why: The thermal scan changes the pre-start plan to an exact 90-minute terminal repair and requires creation of a terminal-repair work-order commitment.

fix_instructions:
Tighten the thresholds for the following checks and facts:
- Increase the minimum number of certified operators required in check C2 to more than two.
- Raise the minimum startup validation sample size in checks C3 and C4 to more than 50 parts.
- Specify a stricter prestart repair time limit in check C6, such as reducing it to 15 minutes.
